review: The decision cites 'a name follows its Gurmukhi spelling' but keeps Krishna, which is ਕ੍ਰਿਸਨ's spelling; ਕਿਸਨੁ is Kisan. Decided: Kisan (Vishnu) / ਕਿਸਨ (ਵਿਸ਼ਨੂੰ) in the line, the note as it stands (it already names Kisan (Krishna)).

issue: Whose are the daggers and the noose (ਤੇਰੇ … ਕਟਾਰੇ ਜੇਵਡਾ)?
our reading: These sights of the Lord's (the Saavan scene) are a dagger and a noose to the bride: they wound her with longing and draw her (the Darpan).
alternatives: The Beloved's glances, sharp as daggers, are ropes that bind (Bhai Vir Singh's Santhya, the Faridkot Teeka: ਕਟਾਖ).
decided because: The stanza opens on the peacocks and Saavan, and the next line (ਤੇਰੇ ਦਰਸਨ ਵਿਟਹੁ) is a sacrifice to the sight of him the bride now sees; the Beloved is absent (he comes only in a dream, line 15), so glances face to face fit less. ਜੇਵਡਾ is ਜੇਵੜਾ, a rope or noose (Darpan, Santhya), not "as great as".

issue: ਤੈ ਸਹ (also line 9, and 557.3 lines 10 and 18 ਤੈ ਸਹ, ਤੈ ਸਾਹਿਬ): you, O Husband, or that Husband?
our reading: You, my Husband / you, my Master, in all four lines.
alternatives: That Husband (the Faridkot Teeka: ਤਿਸ ਪਤੀ; the Darpan at 557.3 line 10: ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਪਤੀ ਨੂੰ).
decided because: ਤੈ is the Lahndi ਤੈਂ, and the Granth's meanings already read ਤੈ ਸਹਿ as you, my Husband Lord (518.6, 520.1, 521.4); the Darpan reads you at 557.2 lines 7 and 9 and at 557.3 line 18, and the bride addresses the Beloved directly in 557.3 line 16. One reading is kept for the one form.

issue: ਜੀ at the end of the Rahao line.
our reading: An address of affection to the bride's friend: dear friend / ਹੇ ਸਖੀ.
alternatives: O sister (the Darpan: ਹੇ ਭੈਣ); O friends (the Faridkot Teeka).
decided because: The soul-bride is speaking to her companions of her Husband (ਮੇਰਾ ਕੰਤੁ), as in 557.3 (ਭੈਣੇ, ਅੰਮਾਲੀ); friend keeps the address without choosing a kinship the word does not name.

issue: A statement or a condition: I ask the way but do not walk it, and say I have arrived.
our reading: A statement of the bride's own state, leading to the question of line 7.
alternatives: If I ask the way but never walk it … (the Darpan, conditional).
decided because: No ਜੇ in the line; the verbs are plain first-person present (ਦਸਾਈ, ਜੁਲਾਂ, ਆਖਾਂ), and line 7 asks how such a one can dwell in the house.

issue: ਗੁਰਮਤਿ ਕਰਣੀ ਸਾਰੁ: ਸਾਰੁ the best (do the best deed by the Guru's teaching) or the imperative of ਸਾਰਨਾ (keep, carry out)?
our reading: Keep to the way of life of the Guru's teaching: ਸਾਰੁ imperative, ਕਰਣੀ the conduct.
alternatives: By the Guru's teaching do the excellent deed (the Faridkot Teeka, Sant Singh Khalsa).
decided because: The Darpan's grammar (ਸਾਰੁ, ਸੰਭਾਲ), and the line is the Rahao's command to the mind, beside ਰਵਹਿ in the next line; 559.4 line 9 is read the same way.

issue: ਕਿਸਨੁ: Krishna or Vishnu?
our reading: Krishna (Vishnu): the name as the line has it, with Vishnu in brackets, and a note.
alternatives: Vishnu alone (the Darpan, the Faridkot Teeka); Krishna alone.
decided because: The stanza names the three gods (Brahma, Mahadev, then Kisan), so the commentators read Vishnu; ਅਵਤਾਰੀ ਰੂਧਾ (caught up in incarnations) fits Vishnu, of whom Krishna is an incarnation. A name follows its Gurmukhi spelling, so Krishna stays in the text.

issue: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ … ਪਰਵਾਰੈ ਸਾਧਾਰੁ: the Gurmukh (a person) is the support of his family, or through the Guru (one becomes) a support.
our reading: Through the Guru, O Nanak, (one becomes) a support to (one's) family too.
alternatives: The Gurmukh is a support to his family (the Darpan, the Faridkot Teeka, Sant Singh Khalsa).
decided because: The settled rendering of ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ as an adverb, through the Guru, held through this litany shabad as everywhere; the sense, that the one who turns to the Guru supports the family, is the same. Line 7 alone, where the Gurmukh is what one becomes (ਸੋ ਹੋਇ), takes the noun.

issue: ਧੋਖਾ: anxiety, doubt or fear?
our reading: Anxiety (ਚਿੰਤਾ).
alternatives: Doubt (the Faridkot Teeka: ਸੰਦੇਹ; Sant Singh Khalsa); fear, dread (the Darpan: ਸਹਮ).
decided because: In Gurbani ਧੋਖਾ is the worry that gnaws at the mind (ਧੋਖਾ ਨਹ ਵਿਆਪਤ); it is lifted by praise and prayer, which fits the inner unrest of the thirsty soul of line 8.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ … ਮੈ ਅਵਰੁ ਨ ਜਾਣਾ: O Nanak, I know … or Nanak knows …
our reading: I, Nanak, know none but the One.
alternatives: O Nanak, I know no other (Sant Singh Khalsa); Nanak knows no other.
decided because: Nanak speaks of himself (§12), and the line has its own ਮੈ; the Granth's meanings render such a line with I, Nanak (34.2).

issue: ਮੈ ਕਰਮਹੀਣ ਕਬ ਹੀ ਗਲਿ ਲਾਵੈ: a question or a statement?
our reading: A question of longing: will he ever clasp me, the luckless one, to his bosom?
alternatives: A statement: he clasps one as luckless as me only rarely (the Darpan).
decided because: ਕਬ ਹੀ is ever/at some time; the stanza runs on the bride's despairing questions (ਹਉ ਕਿਆ ਕਰੀ, line 8), and the Faridkot Teeka and both English references read the longing question.

issue: ਹਰਿ ਗੋਸਟਿ: union with the Lord, or talk of the Lord?
our reading: To hear of the Lord (talk of the Lord), asked of the Guru.
alternatives: Union with the Lord (the Darpan's ਮਿਲਾਪ, glossing (the talk of) union); the Lord's discourse (the Faridkot Teeka's ਕਥਾ).
decided because: ਗੋਸਟਿ is converse (Skt goṣṭhī); one asks for a discourse, and the Darpan itself supplies ਦੀਆਂ ਗੱਲਾਂ; ਕਰਿ ਸਾਂਝੀ is fellowship (Darpan: ਸੰਗਤਿ).

issue: ਸੁਹਾਵੀ ਕਉਣੁ ਸੁ ਵੇਲਾ: an exclamation (how lovely is that moment!) or a question?
our reading: A question: which is that lovely (hour), that moment, in which God is met?
alternatives: An exclamation (the Darpan: ਉਹ ਕੈਸਾ ਸੋਹਣਾ ਸਮਾ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ!).
decided because: ਕਉਣੁ is which; the shabad longs for a meeting not yet had until stanza 4, and the Faridkot Teeka reads the question. ਸੁਹਾਵੀ is feminine (ਘੜੀ implied, as the Darpan says), so both the hour and the moment are kept.

issue: ਕਰਉ ਜਤਨ ਜੇ ਹੋਇ ਮਿਹਰਵਾਨਾ: who becomes kind, and is ਜੇ if or so that?
our reading: I strive that he (the friend who tears the veil, line 12) may be kind to me; to him I would give my soul (line 14).
alternatives: Only if the Lord is kind can I make the effort (Manmohan Singh, Sant Singh Khalsa).
decided because: Lines 12–14 are one thought: the friend who removes the veil, the effort to win his kindness, and the soul given to him (ਤਾ ਕਉ). The Darpan reads it so; ਜੇ as so that is its sense elsewhere in this raag (561.2 line 6).

issue: ਰਤਨ ਜਵਾਹਰ ਹਰਿ ਮਾਣਕ ਲਾਲਾ: the Lord is the jewels, or the Lord's praise is?
our reading: The Lord (is) jewels, gems, pearls and rubies.
alternatives: The words of the Lord's praise are (as) jewels (the Darpan); the four are dispassion, realisation, reflection and love (the Faridkot Teeka).
decided because: The line names only ਹਰਿ beside the jewels; nothing in it supplies praise, so the plain reading is kept.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਦਾਸੁ ਬਖਸੀਸ ਤੁਮਾਰੀ: how does the line run?
our reading: Nanak, your servant, (looks for) your grace.
alternatives: This is your gift to Nanak your servant (Sant Singh Khalsa); for me, your servant, this is your gift (the Faridkot Teeka).
decided because: ਦਾਸੁ is nominative, in apposition to Nanak; the Darpan supplies the hope for grace, which follows the prayer of the shabad (the Name the support of mind and body).

issue: ਲੋਚਾ ਮਿਲਣ ਕੀ ਪਿਆਰੇ: is ਪਿਆਰੇ the one longed for, or an address?
our reading: An address: within me is a longing to meet (him), O dear one; how shall I find the perfect Guru?
alternatives: The longing to meet the Beloved (the Faridkot Teeka, Sant Singh Khalsa).
decided because: After ਮਿਲਣ ਕੀ the -e form stands as a vocative (the Darpan: ਹੇ ਪਿਆਰੇ!), and the shabad addresses companions throughout (ਅੰਮਾਲੀ, ਸਜਣ, ਭਾਈ); the one to be met is left implied, as the line leaves it.

issue: ਪਿਰੁ ਰਾਵੇ ਭਾਇ ਪਿਆਰੇ (line 3): who enjoys whom?
our reading: The Husband (ਪਿਰੁ, subject of the third-person ਰਾਵੇ) delights in the bride for her love and affection; line 2's address continues.
alternatives: She who stays merged in the Shabad enjoys the beloved Husband with love (the Faridkot Teeka, third person); you enjoy the Husband (both English references, against the verb's person).
decided because: ਰਾਵੇ cannot be second person (ਰਾਵਹਿ is, line 21); with line 2 read as an address (decided in the writer's doubts), the Darpan's reading keeps both the address and the grammar.

issue: ਉਦਕੁ ਗੰਗਾ ਵਾਣੀ (line 51): like the Ganga's water, or (your) Bani is (pure as) Ganga water?
our reading: She moves about rapt, like the waters of the Ganga (kept).
alternatives: Your Bani is pure as Ganga water (the Faridkot Teeka); ਵਾਣੀ = the Bani of praise (the Darpan's gloss, though its meaning closes with: as the water of the Ganga).
decided because: The Shabdarth reads ਵਾਣੀ as like (ਗੰਗਾ ਦੇ ਪਾਣੀ ਵਾਕਰ), and the Darpan's meaning ends on the same likeness; the piece stands.

issue: ਸਾਚੇ ਨਾਮ ਵਿਟਹੁ ਬਲਿ ਜਾਉ: the Guru's own I am a sacrifice, or a command to the mind?
our reading: A command to the mind: be a sacrifice to the True Name.
alternatives: I am a sacrifice to the True Name, O my mind (ਜਾਉ as first person, as at line 15).
decided because: The Rahao's second line addresses the mind in the second person (ਰਹਹਿ, ਪਾਵਹਿ: if you remain … you will obtain); the Darpan and the Faridkot Teeka read the command.

issue: Whose inner being and praise are true?
our reading: The Gurmukhs' of line 13 (their inner being, their mind, the praise they sing), and in line 15 they praise in the true place.
alternatives: The Guru's own (the Darpan: through the Guru my heart has become true).
decided because: Lines 12–15 run on in the third person plural (ਆਵਹਿ, ਜਾਵਹਿ, ਪਾਹਿ, ਹਹਿ, ਸਮਾਹਿ); only the closing ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਬਲਿਹਾਰੈ ਜਾਉ turns to the first person. The Faridkot Teeka reads it so.

issue: ਜਿੰਨਿ ਆਪੁ ਉਪਾਇਆ: you who created yourself, or who created (me / all)?
our reading: O you who brought yourself into being.
alternatives: You who created me (one reading of the Santhya); you who created the whole world (the Faridkot Teeka).
decided because: ਆਪੁ with aunkar is the self as object (oneself); nothing in the line supplies me or the world. The Darpan reads it so.

issue: ਮਨਹਿ ਕਹਣਾ: say it to your own mind, or (complaint) is forbidden (Persian manʿ)?
our reading: What you would say is to be said to your own mind, not voiced aloud in complaint.
alternatives: Speaking (of complaint) is forbidden (the Darpan and the Faridkot Teeka read ਮਨਹਿ as ਮਨ੍ਹਾ).
decided because: Two lines earlier in the same chhant ਮਨਹਿ is the mind (ਨਾਮੁ ਮੀਠਾ ਮਨਹਿ ਲਾਗਾ); the line pairs ਸਹਣਾ and ਮਨਹਿ ਕਹਣਾ as two things to do, and the Santhya reads it so. Either reading forbids the spoken complaint.

issue: ਇਕੁ ਕਰਮੁ ਧਰਮੁ ਨ ਹੋਇ ਸੰਜਮੁ ਜਾਮਿ ਨ ਏਕੁ ਪਛਾਣੀ: who fails, and how?
our reading: Not one rite, religious duty or discipline avails, so long as I do not recognise the One.
alternatives: Some do not do good deeds or self-restraint and do not know the One (both English references).
decided because: ਇਕੁ qualifies the rites (not one), not the people (ਇਕਿ would be some); ਜਾਮਿ is until (the Santhya); ਪਛਾਣੀ is first person. The Darpan, the Faridkot Teeka and the Santhya read it so.

issue: ਕਰਹੁ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਲੇਹੁ ਜਮਹੁ ਉਬਾਰੇ: a prayer, or a statement that God saves his devotees?
our reading: A prayer: by the Guru's grace show (us) mercy and save (us) from Jam.
alternatives: A statement: by the Guru's grace you show mercy and save them from Jam (the Darpan and both English references).
decided because: ਕਰਹੁ and ਲੇਹੁ are imperative forms, as ਕਰਹੁ ਦਇਆ in line 1 of this chhant; the Faridkot Teeka reads the prayer.

issue: ਸਹਸਾ ਏਹੁ ਚੁਕਾਵਹੇ: a statement or a plea (remove this dread)?
our reading: A statement: you have made pain and hunger in the world, and (you) take this dread away.
alternatives: A plea: rid me of this dread (the Faridkot Teeka, both English references).
decided because: ਚੁਕਾਵਹੇ is ਚੁਕਾਵਹਿ, the present second person, the same form as ਬੁਝਾਵਹੇ in line 36 and ਚੁਕਾਵਹੇ in line 30, both statements; the Darpan reads it so.

issue: ਕ੍ਰਿਸਨ ਮਾਲਾ ਜਪਹੁ: Krishna's garland worn, or tell the rosary?
our reading: Cast in gold, (wearing) Krishna's garland: meditate (on him), O friends.
alternatives: Tell the rosary of (the Lord) (the Darpan, taking ਮਾਲਾ with ਜਪਹੁ).
decided because: The stanza describes the Beloved's form (eyes, teeth, nose, hair, golden body), and the garland continues it; the Santhya, the Faridkot Teeka and both English references read the garland worn.

issue: Stanzas 7–8: whose beauty is described?
our reading: The Lord's, addressed as you (ਤੇਰੇ), as in stanzas 1–6; lines 50–51 speak of him and of the bride steeped in him in the third person, as the line has it.
alternatives: The Darpan: the beauty of the beings God has made, all his own; the Santhya considers and rejects a personal Guru or Vishnu.
decided because: The pronouns (ਤੇਰੇ, ਤੇਰੀ) are the same as in the stanzas addressed to the Lord, and Nanak's closing prayer is addressed to him; nothing is added to the lines.

issue: ਮੁਈਏ: dear one, or O soul inviting spiritual death?
our reading: dear one (a fond address), with a note.
alternatives: O soul bringing spiritual death on yourself (the Darpan); O mortal bride (both English references).
decided because: The word addresses the bride who is praised (ਰੰਗਿ ਰਤੀ, ਸੋਭਾਵੰਤੀ), so a reproach does not fit; the Faridkot Teeka and the Santhya read ਪਿਆਰੀਏ.

issue: Address or statement: you are a glorious bride, or the bride steeped in her Husband's love is glorious?
our reading: An address: steeped in your Husband's love, dear one, you are a bride full of glory.
alternatives: A statement (the Faridkot Teeka: the woman steeped in her Husband's love is glorious).
decided because: ਨਾਰੇ is vocative, like ਮੁਈਏ; the Darpan and the Santhya read the address.

issue: Where the one note on the closing ਰਾਮ goes.
our reading: At 567.1, the raag's first chhant whose lines close with ਰਾਮ.
alternatives: At 565.2, the raag's first chhant by heading.
decided because: 565.2 and 566.1 have no closing ਰਾਮ; a note there would speak of a word the reader does not see. The note's wording is the one already used (435.14, 537.3).

issue: ਹੁਕਮੇ ਮੰਨਿ ਵਡਿਆਈ: accepting the Hukam, or (keeping the Hukam) in the mind?
our reading: In accepting the Hukam lies glory.
alternatives: Living in the Hukam with it in the mind, one gains glory (the Darpan: ਮੰਨਿ = ਮਨਿ).
decided because: Both readings make acceptance of the Hukam the source of glory; the Faridkot Teeka reads ਮੰਨਿ as accepting, and line 20 goes on to understanding the Hukam.

issue: ਜਗ ਮਹਿ ਖਟਿਆ ਆਇ: who has earned?
our reading: Only the one who meets the True Guru and meditates on the Name (line 14) has earned (the profit) by coming into the world.
alternatives: I have earned merit by coming (Manmohan Singh); one must earn the right to come into the world (Sant Singh Khalsa).
decided because: Lines 13–14 make one sentence: line 14 names who earns; the Darpan reads it so.

review: The doubt says batches 01–02 do not gloss Sant and so glosses it here; batch 02 already uses Sant (562.1 line 15, 563.2 line 6), so any gloss in this raag belongs there, not at 569.2.
reviewer_fix: No gloss at 569.2; Sant's one gloss in Raag Vadhans, if any, is at its first place, 562.1 line 15, as the Granth's meanings word it: Sants (saints).

issue: Line 11, ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਰਾਮ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਏ: ਗਾਏ is not a first-person finite verb, yet the piece reads (I) sing.
our reading: Kept: ਗਾਏ as the conjunct participle (ਗਾਇ, singing), as ਲਾਏ in 570.1 line 24; in union with the Guru's Sikhs, singing the Lord's praises night and day, my longing is fulfilled, which the piece's (and I) sing carries without change of sense.
alternatives: Third person: (one who joins them) sings (the Darpan); the Gursikh who sings night and day (the Santhya); a prayer, so that I may sing (the Faridkot Teeka).
decided because: The participle reading is grammatical and keeps the one speaker of the shabad; the piece is not wrong enough to change for it.

issue: ਜੋ ਭਾਵੈ ਸੋ ਭੁੰਚਿ ਤੂ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਨਦਰਿ ਨਿਹਾਲਿ (and line 9): an imperative, or a promise; and whose sight is ਨਦਰਿ?
our reading: Imperative: take for your food whatever pleases (God), and through the Guru behold with (inner) sight (lines 8 and 9 alike; line 9 goes on: within you is the Lord's Name, your friend).
alternatives: The Darpan: make God's will your food, look with the eyes of the Gurmukhs; the Faridkot Teeka: becoming Gurmukh and beholding the Lord, you will enjoy whatever you wish.
decided because: ਭੁੰਚਿ and ਨਿਹਾਲਿ are imperatives (the stanza is a string of commands to the mind: ਨ ਭਾਲਿ); ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ is read adverbially as the Granth's meanings settle it; the next line places what is to be seen within, so (inner) sight is the implied sense without naming whose eyes.

issue: ਜੀਉ at the end of lines 1 and 2, and ਰਾਮ at the end of chhant lines throughout 569.1–572.2.
our reading: Not rendered: sung endings of the measure.
alternatives: ਜੀਉ as an address (dear one) or as the soul.
decided because: The settled rule leaves the closing ਰਾਮ of chhant lines unrendered with one note in the raag; that note belongs to the raag's first chhant with ਰਾਮ (567.1, batch 03), so none is repeated here. Line-final ਜੀਉ is left unrendered as the Granth's meanings leave it (73.1, line 2).

issue: Who is the feminine subject of ਵਿਗੁਤੀ … ਮੋਹੀ?
our reading: The manmukh world (ਲੁਕਾਈ) is ruined and held fast in attachment by Jamkaal.
alternatives: The manmukh's intellect (the Faridkot Teeka: ਬੁਧੀ).
decided because: The Darpan supplies ਲੁਕਾਈ, which fits line 11 (ਸਭ ਬਾਧੀ ਜਮਕਾਲਿ, all the world bound) and the Granth's rendering of that phrase (30.1, 31.3).

issue: Who is the ਪਨਿਹਾਰੀ, the water-drawer?
our reading: The attention (ਸੁਰਤ), drawing Amrit from the well within through the Shabad.
alternatives: The intellect (the Faridkot Teeka: ਬੁਧੀ); left unnamed (the Shabad OS English).
decided because: The Darpan names the ਸੁਰਤ; the image needs a drawer within the person, and attention and intellect differ little here; one bracket keeps the image plain.

issue: ਸਚਿ ਸਵਾਰਣਹਾਰਾ.
our reading: The Adorner (the Lord) adorns him with Truth.
alternatives: He adorns his own life through the True Name (the Darpan); the True Lord is his adorner (the Faridkot Teeka).
decided because: ਸਵਾਰਣਹਾਰਾ is an agent noun (the one who adorns), which fits God, and ਸਚਿ with sihari is instrumental (with Truth); the readings agree that the Gurmukh is adorned through Truth.

issue: ਭਜਿ ਪਏ (plural): who ran to the Lord's refuge?
our reading: (I) have run to the Lord's refuge: the speaker, who prays in the next line.
alternatives: Those who run to the refuge are saved (the Darpan, third person); we, or the Gurmukhs (the Faridkot Teeka).
decided because: Line 14 continues in the first person (ਅਰਦਾਸਿ ਕਰੀਂ), and the plural is the humble first person, as with ਸੇਵਹ, ਸਰੇਵਹ, ਲਾਗਹ in 572.1–572.2, which are rendered I; the Granth's meanings render such plurals I.

issue: Whom does ਤੁਧੁ (you) address: the Guru of line 14 or the Lord?
our reading: Left as you, no name added.
alternatives: The Guru (the Faridkot Teeka: ਹੇ ਗੁਰੋ); the Lord (the Darpan's next line).
decided because: The line itself does not say; the prayer is made before the Guru for the Lord's Name, and either reading is the same plea.

issue: ਮਤਿ ਪਰਵਾਣੁ ਸਚੁ ਸਾਈ.
our reading: That understanding (of theirs) is approved by the True One.
alternatives: That understanding is true and approved (the Shabad OS English); that alone is the approved understanding (the Faridkot Teeka).
decided because: ਸਚੁ with aunkar is a noun in the direct case (the True One), as the Darpan reads it; ਸਾਈ (that same) goes with the feminine ਮਤਿ.

issue: ਬੈਰਾਗੁ / ਬੈਰਾਗੀ: renunciation, or longing?
our reading: Bairag (longing for the Lord) has arisen; the longing (mind) finds peace meeting the Guru.
alternatives: The mind has renounced the world (the Shabad OS English; the Faridkot Teeka: a mind fit for detachment).
decided because: The stanza is a cry to be brought to the Guru (lines 14–19); the Darpan reads ਬੈਰਾਗੁ as the longing to meet; the Granth's meanings render bairag as longing for the Lord (29.2).

issue: ਹਰਿ ਪੁਰਖੁ ਨਿਰੰਜਨੁ ਸੋਈ: does the Guru give the gift of the Lord who is the Purakh, or is the Guru himself that Purakh?
our reading: (The Guru) gives the gift of the Lord, who is the Purakh, the all-pervading Being, Niranjan.
alternatives: The True Guru is himself the Niranjan Purakh (the Faridkot Teeka); He (the Lord) is the Immaculate (the Shabad OS English).
decided because: The Darpan reads ਸੋਈ of the Lord whose gift is given; it keeps the plain distinction of giver and gift in the line and needs no identification the line does not state.

issue: ਗੁਰਸਿਖ ਮੇਲਿ ਮੇਰੀ ਸਰਧਾ ਪੂਰੀ: a statement, or a prayer (unite me with the Gursikhs, fulfil my longing)?
our reading: In union with the Guru's Sikhs my longing is fulfilled, and night and day (I) sing the Lord's praises.
alternatives: A prayer to the Lord (the Faridkot Teeka: unite me with the Gursikhs and fulfil my longing, so that I sing).
decided because: ਪੂਰੀ is the participle (fulfilled), not the imperative ਪੂਰਿ of line 10; ਮੇਲਿ is read as locative (in union with), as the Darpan reads it in its explanation.

issue: The speaker's gender in the Punjabi.
our reading: Feminine throughout 572.2 (ਕਰਦੀ ਹਾਂ, ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹਾਂ, ਜੀਉਂਦੀ), as the first stanza marks it (ਨਿਮਾਣੀ, ਢੂਢੇਦੀ, ਸਮਾਣੀ, ਪਛਾਣੀ); 572.1 has no feminine form and stays masculine.
alternatives: The Darpan turns to the masculine in stanzas 2 and 3.
decided because: One speaker runs through the shabad, and the verse itself marks her as the soul-bride.

issue: ਕਰਮਿ ਬਿਧਾਤਾ: by grace, or according to deeds?
our reading: The Maker (of beings) according to (their) deeds.
alternatives: The Creator who gives by grace (ਕਰਮ as grace elsewhere in Gurbani).
decided because: The Darpan, the Faridkot Teeka and the Shabad OS English agree on deeds, and the Granth's meanings already render the same phrase so (126.2).

issue: Heading ਵਡਹੰਸੁ ਮਹਲਾ ੪ ਛੰਤ: Chhant or Chhants.
our reading: Raag Vadhans, Chhants, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
alternatives: a Chhant (singular).
decided because: The heading stands over a set (572.1 is ॥੪॥੧॥ and 572.2 ॥੪॥੨॥ follows), as the Granth's meanings render Raag Gauri, Chhants (247.1); batch 03's ਵਡਹੰਸੁ ਮਹਲਾ ੩ ਛੰਤ (567.1) should match.

issue: Gloss of Sant.
our reading: the Sants (the holy), glossed here.
alternatives: No gloss, if an earlier batch of this raag (03) has already glossed it.
decided because: Batches 01–02 do not gloss Sant; reviewers keep only the first gloss in the raag.

review: The doubt credits the Darpan with a vocative ਮੇਰੇ ਰਾਮ; the Darpan's address comes from ਜੀ (ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਜੀ!) and it leaves ਰਾਮ unrendered. The decision changes with the fix above.

reviewer_fix.issue: ਮੇਰੇ ਰਾਮ at the line's end.
reviewer_fix.our reading: ਮੇਰੇ goes with ਜੀ as the address, O my dear (Lord); the closing ਰਾਮ is left unrendered, as in every chhant line of the raag.
reviewer_fix.alternatives: Render ਮੇਰੇ ਰਾਮ as a full vocative, O my Lord (Sant Singh Khalsa).
reviewer_fix.decided because: ਮੇਰੇ is masculine and cannot go with the feminine ਆਸਾ ਮਨਸਾ, so it is an address; with ਜੀ it is complete, and the Lord addressed is clear from lines 21-23. This keeps the raag's rule for the closing ਰਾਮ and accounts for every word, as 547.1 (ਸੁਆਮੀ ਮੇਰੇ ਰਾਮ) does; the Darpan takes its address from ਜੀ (ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਜੀ!).

issue: ਮੇਰੇ ਲਾਥੇ ਜੀ ਸਗਲ ਵਿਸੂਰੇ: whom ਜੀ addresses.
our reading: The Lord (dear Lord), as line 20's ਜੀ and line 21's ਜੀਉ in the same stanza.
alternatives: The listeners (O brothers); Faridkot: ਮੇਰੇ ਜੀ = my mind, from which the sorrows have gone.
decided because: The whole stanza speaks to the Lord (ਤੇਰੇ, ਠਾਕੁਰ ਮੇਰੇ, ਤੁਧੁ ਸਾਲਾਹੀ, ਬਖਸਿ ਲੀਆ), and the Darpan reads ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਜੀ! here; in stanza 1 (line 2) the Darpan's ਹੇ ਭਾਈ stands.

issue: ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ … ਨ ਕਰੀਅਹੁ: who is addressed.
our reading: An appeal to the listeners (ਕਰੀਅਹੁ is second person plural): for the Lord's sake, never look upon those who have not meditated on the Name.
alternatives: Faridkot and Sant Singh Khalsa: O Lord, let me not see them.
decided because: The verb is a second-person plural command, not a request to the Lord to cause (me) to see; the Darpan reads it so.

issue: ਹਰਿ ਸਤੀ
our reading: ਸਤੀ = ਸਤਿ, the ever-true Lord, whose Name the Guru made firm.
alternatives: Faridkot: ਸਤੀ = contented (we, becoming content, utter the Name).
decided because: The line has no first-person subject for 'we become content'; ਹਰਿ ਸਤੀ stands with the Name as its object, as the Darpan reads it.

issue: ਹਮ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਕਰਹ ਭਗਤੀ: whose worship.
our reading: I may worship the True Guru (and in line 21 the True Guru and the Lord).
alternatives: Darpan: meeting the Guru, I will worship the Lord.
decided because: The words name the True Guru as the object of the devotion; line 21 puts the Lord, Har Har, beside him.

issue: ਸੋਈ ਭਗਤੁ: who.
our reading: General: he alone is a devotee who holds pain and pleasure the same.
alternatives: Darpan: that (Guru) alone is the true devotee.
decided because: Nothing in the line ties ਸੋਈ to the Guru of the previous line; the general sense includes the Guru and stays with the words.

issue: ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮਿ ਉਧਾਰੇ
our reading: The Name has saved servant Nanak (Nanak speaks of himself).
alternatives: Darpan: O Nanak, those who tasted the Lord's savour are saved by the Name.
decided because: ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ stands as the one saved, and the first half (meeting the True Guru, I found the savour) has the same speaker.

issue: ਬੁਝਿ ਚੰਗਾ
our reading: Understanding the Good One (God), I put the saddle on the body.
alternatives: Darpan: reflecting on (God's) goodnesses; Sant Singh Khalsa: the saddle of realising the Good Lord.
decided because: ਬੁਝਿ is a conjunct participle and ਚੰਗਾ its object; Santhya explains the saddle as knowing the Lord to be the best of all.

issue: ਭੁਇਅੰਗਾ
our reading: The (world-) ocean.
alternatives: A serpent (ਭੁਜੰਗ), the world as a coiled snake (Santhya's first sense).
decided because: The next line gives it endless waves and a crossing by ship; the Darpan and Santhya's second sense read the ocean.

issue: ਹਰਿ ਰੰਗੁ ਤੁਰੀ ਚੜਾਇਆ
our reading: He has put the Lord's colour on the mare (dyed the body with the Lord's love).
alternatives: Darpan: he mounts the (body-) mare, bringing it under control.
decided because: ਰੰਗੁ is the object of ਚੜਾਇਆ (to put a colour on), as Santhya reads it; the dyeing image runs through these chhants (ਰੰਗੁ ਚਲੂਲਾ, ਨਵ ਰੰਗੜੀਆ).

issue: ਧੁਰਿ ਪਾਇਆ ਕਿਰਤੁ ਜੁੜੰਦਾ
our reading: The mare (the human body) is gained as ordained from the first, by the deeds of the past gathered together.
alternatives: Darpan: through it the gathered impressions of past deeds come to light.
decided because: Santhya and Sant Singh Khalsa read it of how the body is obtained, which fits ਪਾਇਆ with the mare as its object.

issue: ਕਤਹਿ ਨ ਜਾਇਆ … ਸੰਗਿ ਬੈਸਾ: whose going and sitting.
our reading: The finder: having found God, I go nowhere else and abide with him for ever.
alternatives: God, who never goes away and ever sits with (me).
decided because: The stanza is told by the one who received the Shabad; ਕਤਹਿ (to any other place) reads naturally of the seeker no longer wandering, as the Darpan takes it.

issue: Subject of ਪ੍ਰਭ ਜੀ ਭਾਣਾ.
our reading: General: whoever is pleasing to God has true honour; God has given him the Lord's wealth.
alternatives: First person, continuing lines 10-11 (I have become pleasing to God).
decided because: Line 13 is a sacrifice to that servant (ਤਿਸੁ ਜਨ), which needs the one pleasing to God in line 12 to be a third person.

issue: ਮੇਰੇ ਰਾਮ at the line's end.
our reading: An address, O my dear Lord (ਮੇਰੇ cannot go with the feminine ਆਸਾ ਮਨਸਾ).
alternatives: Leave ਰਾਮ unrendered as the chhant's closing word and read ਮੇਰੇ with the hopes.
decided because: Grammar: ਮੇਰੇ is masculine and so goes with ਰਾਮ, making a vocative, as the Darpan and Sant Singh Khalsa read it.

issue: ਲੋਈ
our reading: The world: with my eyes I have seen the world, yet the thirst does not go.
alternatives: Sant Singh Khalsa: the Light of the Lord.
decided because: The second line contrasts these eyes with the other eyes that see the Beloved, which needs the first to have seen only the world; the Darpan glosses ਲੋਈ as ਜਗਤ.

issue: ਜੋ ਲੋੜੀਦੇ ਰਾਮ
our reading: Those whom the Lord wants (ਲੋੜੀਦੇ passive) are called his servants.
alternatives: Sant Singh Khalsa: those who long for the Lord.
decided because: ਲੋੜੀਦੇ is a passive form (are wanted), with ਰਾਮ as the one who wants them; the Darpan reads it so.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਜਾਣੇ ਸਤਿ
our reading: Nanak knows it to be true (ਜਾਣੇ, third person).
alternatives: Darpan: O Nanak, know it as true (taking ਜਾਣੇ as ਜਾਣਿ).
decided because: ਜਾਣੇ as written is the third-person present; the imperative would be ਜਾਣਿ or ਜਾਣੁ.

issue: ਗਾਵਹੁ ਗੀਤੁ ਨ ਬਿਰਹੜਾ (line 33): sing no song of separation, or sing (God's) song so there is no separation?
our reading: Sing no song of separation; (sing) the contemplation of God.
alternatives: Sing the song of contemplating God, and there will be no separation again (the Darpan, the Faridkot Teeka).
decided because: ਨ stands with ਗੀਤੁ ... ਬਿਰਹੜਾ, and the shabad turns the dirge (ਰੋਵਹੁ, line 21) into praise of the Husband (lines 29 to 32); the reading keeps the words' order, and the meaning of the alternative (praise in place of lament) is carried by (sing) the contemplation of God.

issue: ਰਖਿ ਲੇਹੁ: a prayer (save us) or a statement (you save)?
our reading: A prayer: removing doubt, pain and suffering, save (us), O merciful to the meek.
alternatives: A statement: you save (all beings), removing their pain in an instant (the Darpan).
decided because: ਲੇਹੁ is the imperative form, and the chhant opens in petition (ਰਖੁ ਜਗਤੁ ਸਗਲ, line 2).

issue: ਦਰਿ: at whose door does the unstruck music play?
our reading: At (his) door: the Lord's door, as in line 24, left open as the line leaves it.
alternatives: In the heart (the Darpan: ਦਰਿ, ਹਿਰਦੇ ਵਿਚ).
decided because: The line names no heart; (his) keeps the plain sense without adding a reading the words do not state.

issue: ਰੋਵਹ ਬਿਰਹਾ ਤਨ ਕਾ: whose separation?
our reading: Let us weep over the parting of the body (the words as they stand), and keep the Master in mind.
alternatives: Weep over our separation from God (the Darpan); weep over the separation from God that the body's leanings cause (Bhai Vir Singh's Santhya).
decided because: ਤਨ ਕਾ binds the separation to the body; in a dirge the parting of the body is death, which the next line ties to our own going (ਅਸਾ ਭਿ ਓਥੈ ਜਾਣਾ). The plain words are kept.

issue: ਤਿਨਿ: the departed one, or God?
our reading: What the departed one did and gathered has come before him.
alternatives: What God ordained has come to pass (some, noted by the Santhya).
decided because: The Darpan and the Santhya both take ਤਿਨਿ as the departed, which matches 578.2 line 6 (ਜੇਹਾ ਪੁਰਬਿ ਕਮਾਇਆ).

issue: ਦੇਹਿ ਪਿਆਰੋ (Rahao): a prayer (give me love) or a statement (you give love)?
our reading: A statement: you give true love.
alternatives: A prayer: give me your true love (the Faridkot Teeka, Sant Singh Khalsa).
decided because: The same verb in line 8 (ਦੇਹਿ ਜੀਆ ਆਧਾਰੋ) is a statement on every reading; the Rahao praises the Master as the Darpan reads it.

issue: ਤੂ ਥਿਰੁ ਕਰਣੈਹਾਰੋ: you, the Maker, are eternal, or you make (the soul) steady?
our reading: You created coming and going; you, the Maker, are eternal.
alternatives: You make the soul steady, freeing it from coming and going (the Santhya; the Faridkot Teeka's second reading).
decided because: The contrast with the created coming and going is the Lord's own permanence (the Darpan, Faridkot's first reading); nothing in the line names the soul.

issue: ਸਾ ਧਨ: the widow, or the body (bride of the soul)?
our reading: The wife left alone, widowed, with the corpse in the courtyard.
alternatives: The body-bride left by the soul (Sant Singh Khalsa; the Darpan's word gloss).
decided because: The stanza paints the funeral scene (the corpse at the door, the wife weeping at the gate in line 20, her cry in line 24); the Faridkot Teeka and the Darpan's meaning take the widow.

issue: ਪੰਚ: the five nearest kin or the five senses?
our reading: The five nearest kin are as dead, stricken at heart.
alternatives: The five senses went slack (the Faridkot Teeka).
decided because: The scene is the mourners at the bier; the Darpan and the Santhya name the kin (mother, father, brother, wife, son).

issue: ਹਉ ਮੁਠੜੀ: who is robbed, I or you?
our reading: First person: I am robbed, running after worldly business; the Husband has left me.
alternatives: You (the mourners) are robbed and left by the Husband (the Faridkot Teeka, the Santhya).
decided because: ਹਉ is I, and the next line but one goes on in the first person (ਮੈ ਪਿਰੁ ਸਚੁ ਸਾਲਾਹਣਾ ਹਉ ਰਹਸਿਅੜੀ); the Darpan and Sant Singh Khalsa read I.

issue: ਸੋ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਪਰਵਾਣੋ: accept him as Master, or he is the approved Master?
our reading: Accept him as the Master.
alternatives: That Master is the approved one (the Darpan).
decided because: It answers line 1 (ਕੁਦਰਤਿ ਜਾਣੋਵਾ, know); the Santhya and the Faridkot Teeka read the call to accept.

issue: ਮਿਲਹੁ ਸੰਜੋਗੀ: meet in the Sangat, or meet those who join (to the Lord)?
our reading: Meet with those who join (others to the Lord), who have untied their nooses by meeting the Guru.
alternatives: Gather in the Sangat (the Darpan); such friends are met by good fortune (the Santhya's alternative, Sant Singh Khalsa).
decided because: The second half names people who have met the Guru and untied their nooses, the ones to meet; the Santhya and the Faridkot Teeka read ਸੰਜੋਗੀ so.

issue: ਭੈ ਰੋਵੈ ਗੁਣ ਸਾਰਿ ਸਮਾਲੇ: approved weeping, or the mourner's own fear?
our reading: Let one weep in God's fear, cherishing and recalling his virtues; no one dies with the dead.
alternatives: One weeps in fear of his own troubles and recalls the dead one's virtues (the Darpan).
decided because: Line 24 praises those who weep remembering the True One; the Santhya, the Faridkot Teeka and Sant Singh Khalsa read the fear of God.

issue: ਮਰਿ ਜੰਮੈ ਵਾਰੋ ਵਾਰਾ (line 8): who dies and is born, the world of line 7 or the soul-bride?
our reading: (The soul-bride) dies and is born again and again, as the piece has it; kept.
alternatives: The world (ਜਗੁ, line 7; the Darpan: ਜਗਤ … ਮੁੜ ਮੁੜ ਜੰਮਦਾ ਮਰਦਾ, then ਜੀਵ and ਦੁਨੀਆ).
decided because: Line 9 goes on with feminine ਗਿਆਨ ਵਿਹੂਣੀ ਮੂਠੀ and line 10 with ਪਿਰੁ ਨ ਪਾਇਓ … ਅਵਗੁਣਿਆਰੀ, so the one dying and being born is the bride the stanza speaks of (the world as bride); the singular ਜੰਮੈ fits either, and the sense does not change.

issue: ਮੈ ਸਦਾ ਰਾਵੇ ਪਿਰੁ ਆਪਣਾ: who enjoys whom?
our reading: My own Husband ever delights in me (ਪਿਰੁ the subject of ਰਾਵੇ, ਮੈ the object), as I reflect through the True Shabad.
alternatives: I ever enjoy (dwell on) my Husband (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh in English).
decided because: ਰਾਵੇ is third person singular, agreeing with ਪਿਰੁ; a first-person subject would want ਰਾਵਾ / ਰਾਵਉ. The Darpan reads the Husband as subject (ਮੇਰਾ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ-ਪਤੀ ਮੈਨੂੰ ... ਜੋੜੀ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ); ਵੀਚਾਰੇ is ਵੀਚਾਰਿ, having reflected (Darpan).

issue: ਨਾ ਓਹੁ ਮਰੈ ਨ ਜਾਏ (also lines 3 and 18): nor goes away, or nor is born?
our reading: He neither dies nor goes away (does not leave the bride), in all three lines.
alternatives: Neither dies nor is born (the Darpan at lines 13 and 18: ਨਾਹ ਜੰਮਦਾ ਹੈ; at line 3 it reads ਛੱਡ ਕੇ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾਂਦਾ).
decided because: The image is the widow (ਰੰਡ, lines 14–15): the bride's grief is a husband who dies or leaves; ਜਾਏ is the verb to go, as the Darpan itself takes it at line 3. One reading is kept for the one refrain (Sant Singh Khalsa and Manmohan Singh read leave / go too).

issue: ਸਚੈ ਸਰਿ ਨਾਏ ਸਚੈ ਸਹਜਿ ਸੁਭਾਏ: what is the second ਸਚੈ?
our reading: (One) bathes in the true pool, and (abides) in the True One, in Sahaj and in love.
alternatives: Becomes true, with ease (Manmohan Singh, the Faridkot Teeka: ਸਹਜਿ ਸੁਭਾਏ ਨਿਰਜਤਨ ਹੀ ਸਚੇ ਹੈਂ; Sant Singh Khalsa: one becomes truthful).
decided because: ਸਚੈ has the same locative ending as ਸਚੈ ਸਰਿ just before it and as ਸਹਜਿ after; the Darpan reads it as absorption in the True One (ਉਸ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਵਿਚ ਲੀਨ ਹੋ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ).

issue: ਸਾਚਿ ਸਬਦਿ ਧਨ ਰਾਤੀ: the True Shabad, or the True Name and the Shabad?
our reading: The soul-bride stays dyed in the True Shabad.
alternatives: Dyed in the True Name (ਸਾਚਿ) and in the Shabad (ਸਬਦਿ) as two words (the Darpan: ਸਦਾ-ਥਿਰ ਹਰਿ-ਨਾਮ ਵਿਚ ... ਸ਼ਬਦ ਵਿਚ).
decided because: ਸਾਚਿ agrees with ਸਬਦਿ in case, as ਸਚੈ ਸਬਦਿ does in this shabad's line 23 and in 584.1; Sant Singh Khalsa and Manmohan Singh read one phrase too. The sense hardly differs.

issue: ਹਰਿ ਗੁਣਕਾਰੀ: what is ਗੁਣਕਾਰੀ?
our reading: The Lord, the giver of virtues (who works virtue in one).
alternatives: The source of virtues (the Darpan: ਗੁਣਾਂ ਦਾ ਸੋਮਾ); the virtuous one (Sant Singh Khalsa); the Lord's virtues are beautiful (the Faridkot Teeka).
decided because: ਗੁਣਕਾਰੀ is one who does or brings about ਗੁਣ (ਕਾਰੀ, doer), an epithet of ਹਰਿ here; giver of virtues keeps both the word's parts and the Darpan's sense.

issue: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਨਾਮਿ ਨਿਵਾਸੁ: the Gurmukh (noun) or through the Guru (adverb)?
our reading: The Gurmukhs dwell in the Name.
alternatives: Through the Guru, there is dwelling in the Name.
decided because: The line sets the Gurmukh against the manmukhs of the salok (line 5), as the Darpan reads it (ਗੁਰੂ ਦੇ ਸਨਮੁਖ ਰਹਿਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਬੰਦਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਸੁਰਤਿ); the same at 586.1 line 4 (ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਮਨਿ ਵੀਚਾਰਿਆ, the Darpan and the Faridkot Teeka: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਾਂ).

review: ਕਲਿ ਮਹਿ is an open reading with no doubt entry: the Darpan glosses ਕਲਿ as the state of duality, separation from the Lord (ਦੁਬਿਧਾ ਵਾਲਾ ਸੁਭਾਉ, citing ਇਕ ਘੜੀ ਨ ਮਿਲਤੇ ਤ ਕਲਿਜੁਗੁ ਹੋਤਾ), and carries it into line 2 (ਗੁਰੂ ਨੇ 'ਕਲਿ' ਤੋਂ ਬਚਾ ਲਿਆ); Faridkot gives Kalyug first and ਕਲਪਨਾ as an alternative. Kalyug stands (Faridkot, the plain word, Jam's rule over the world in line 3), but the doubt must be recorded, and the Kalyug note depends on it.

issue: ਚਿੰਤ ਪਰਾਈ: hope in another, or anxiety about others' affairs?
our reading: they do not look in the least to another (besides the Lord)
alternatives: no care for others' concerns / no envy
decided because: the Darpan's pad-arth gives ਚਿੰਤ as ਆਸ (hope), ਚੁਖਾ as ਰਤਾ ਭੀ; the review's recast keeps that sense.

issue: ਸਾਧ ਜਨੁ: vocative (O holy people), or in apposition to the True Guru?
our reading: the Saadh, in apposition: that True Guru, the Saadh
alternatives: O holy people (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh)
decided because: ਜਨੁ has aunkar: singular nominative/accusative, so it stands with ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ, not a plural vocative; the Darpan reads ਸਾਧ-ਗੁਰੂ.

issue: ਜਿਥਹੁ ਕੋ ਵਰਸਾਇ: who benefits from the householder?
our reading: someone gains (something) from the householder
alternatives: the householder himself can fulfil his hope (Darpan)
decided because: ਕੋ is someone; Faridkot and the Santhya read others gaining from the householder's earning, which sets the householder against the begging garb-wearer of lines 2–4.

issue: ਪਾਵਹਿ: you (God) accept, or they obtain?
our reading: whose honour you, (O Lord,) accept
alternatives: they have their honour accepted (third plural)
decided because: ਜਿਨ ਕੀ ਪਤਿ is the object; a third-plural subject has no sense here, so ਪਾਵਹਿ is the second person to God (Darpan), the turn to address marked in brackets.

issue: ਸਜਣ ਮਿਲੇ ਸਜਣਾ: who are the friends?
our reading: friends have met friends, left as the line has it
alternatives: the seeker meets the Guru (Faridkot); satsangis meet satsangis (Darpan); the friend meets the Lord (Sant Singh Khalsa)
decided because: the line names no one; line 6 (light merging in the Light) and 587.3 (those who love the True Guru) both fit the plain words, so the meaning keeps them.

issue: ਢੋਈਐ: shelter, or an offering (ਢੋਆ) by which one reaches the court?
our reading: shelter is found in the Lord's court
alternatives: with this offering one reaches the Lord's presence (Darpan)
decided because: ਢੋਈ is shelter wherever else the Granth uses it in our meanings (18.3, 44.1); Faridkot reads shelter or honour.

issue: ਦਰਸਨ: the sight of the Guru or of God?
our reading: the sight (of the Guru)
alternatives: the sight of God (Darpan)
decided because: the salok opens with those who love the True Guru; Faridkot reads the Guru's darshan; the bracket marks it as implied.

issue: ਜਿਸੁ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਫਲ ਹਰਿ ਲਾਗੇ ਮੁਖਾ: the Guru's mouth bears the fruit, or tastes it?
our reading: whose mouth bears the Lord's Amrit fruit
alternatives: whose mouth tastes the fruit (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh)
decided because: ਫਲ ਲਾਗੇ is fruit growing on a tree; the Darpan and Faridkot read the words of praise from the Guru's mouth as the fruit.

issue: ਤਿਸ ਦਾ ਫਰੂ ਨ ਕੋਇ: no protector of the world, or no one to hold back Jam?
our reading: it (the world) has no one to protect it
alternatives: no one can hold him (Jam) back (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh)
decided because: ਤਿਸ follows ਜਗੁ, the subject of the clause; the Darpan and Faridkot gloss ਫਰੂ as protector (ਰਾਖਾ, ਰੱਖਕ).

issue: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ: the adverb through the Guru, or the Gurmukhs?
our reading: Jam serves the Gurmukhs, in whose minds the True One is
alternatives: through the Guru, Jam serves those in whose minds…
decided because: the relative ਜਿਨ needs a plural antecedent, which only ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ supplies; all the commentaries read the Gurmukhs here.

issue: ਵਡ ਪੁੰਨੁ and ਗੁਣੀ
our reading: great is the good done by that True Guru, who has made (me) understand the Lord of virtues
alternatives: great merit accrues to the Guru (Faridkot); has instructed me in virtue (Sant Singh Khalsa)
decided because: the Darpan reads ਪੁੰਨੁ as the Guru's favour (ਉਪਕਾਰ) to beings; the Darpan and Faridkot both read ਗੁਣੀ as the Lord, the treasure of virtues.

issue: ਜਿਸੁ ਤੂ ਭਾਵੈ: whom you will, or to whom you are pleasing?
our reading: whomever you will
alternatives: those to whom you are pleasing (those who love you)
decided because: the Darpan glosses ਭਾਵੈ as ਚਾਹੇਂ, Faridkot as ਚਾਹਤਾ ਹੈਂ; it fits the next half, what (power) have the poor creatures.

issue: ਗੁਰ ਬੁਧਿ ਬੀਚਾਰੀ: the Guru's understanding has seen this, or reflect with the Guru's wisdom?
our reading: so the Guru's understanding has seen
alternatives: reflect upon the Guru's teaching (Sant Singh Khalsa); when I reflect with Guru-given wisdom (Manmohan Singh)
decided because: ਬੀਚਾਰੀ is a perfective with ਗੁਰ ਬੁਧਿ as its agent (Darpan, Faridkot), not a command.

issue: ਜੀਅ ਕੇ ਬੰਧਨਾ ਵਿਚਿ ਹਉਮੈ ਕਰਮ ਕਮਾਹਿ: how the line divides
our reading: deeds done in Haumai are bonds for the soul
alternatives: they act in Haumai within the soul's bonds
decided because: the Darpan's reading; both say that without the Guru action binds.

issue: ਤਿਨਿ (singular ergative): the Guru, or the one in whom the Guru has made the Naam firm?
our reading: The one in whom the Guru has made the Naam firm has shattered Haumai and duality.
alternatives: The Guru implants the Name and (he) stills their ego (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh).
decided because: The Darpan and the Faridkot Teeka take ਤਿਨਿ as the one taught; the pauri praises the Gursikhs throughout, and the next lines keep them as subject.

issue: ਭਾਵੈ ਸਉ ਗੇੜਾ ਆਵਉ ਜਾਉ: come and go to the Guru a hundred times, or a hundred rounds of birth and death?
our reading: though he come and go (to the Guru) a hundred times.
alternatives: even though he come and go (in births) hundreds of times.
decided because: Line 1 speaks of one who has no trust in the True Guru; the Darpan and the Faridkot Teeka both supply (to the Guru): visits without trust bring no peace.

issue: ਅਚਿੰਤੁ: the carefree Lord (an epithet), or naturally, without effort (an adverb)?
our reading: The Name of the carefree Lord has come to dwell in their minds.
alternatives: The Lord's Name naturally fills their minds (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh).
decided because: ਅਚਿੰਤੁ with aunkar is a masculine singular adjective standing before ਹਰਿ; the Darpan and the Faridkot Teeka read it of the Lord (free of care, freeing from care).

issue: ਤਿਨਾ ਸਤਗੁਰੁ ਮਿਲਿਆ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਆਇ: the True Guru and God as two subjects, or the True Guru who is God (apposition)?
our reading: have met the True Guru, and God has come (to meet them).
alternatives: the True Guru, God incarnate, comes and meets them (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh, Faridkot).
decided because: The Darpan reads two steps (the Guru met, then God); either keeps the sense that God is reached through the Guru, and the two-step reading needs no epithet the line does not state.

issue: ਅਗਲੀ ਕਾਣਿ: the former (old) subjection to Jam, or the subjection to come (in the next world)?
our reading: all our old subjection to Jam is gone.
alternatives: the subjection of the next world / future subjection to death (Faridkot, Manmohan Singh).
decided because: With the perfective ਗਈ (has gone) the dependence is one that was there before; the Darpan glosses ਅਗਲੀ as ਪਹਿਲੀ.

issue: ਘਰ ਹੀ ਮੁੰਧਿ ਵਿਦੇਸਿ ਪਿਰੁ: the bride at home and the Husband abroad, or the Husband in the home itself while the bride thinks him abroad?
our reading: The Husband is right at home, (yet) the bride (thinks him) gone abroad.
alternatives: The bride is at home, while the Husband is away (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh).
decided because: Line 2 says there is no delay in meeting once the intention is set right, which needs the Husband near; the Darpan, the Faridkot Teeka and the Santhya all read the Husband in the home (the heart).

issue: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਕੀ ਪਾਖਿਆ: God taking their side, or their taking God's side (his refuge)?
our reading: with God on their side.
alternatives: in the protection (refuge) of God (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh, Faridkot).
decided because: ਪਾਖਿਆ is ਪੱਖ (side, support: the Santhya's Sanskrit pakṣa); the Darpan and the Santhya's first reading are God's taking their side, which also follows from line 1 (the Lord has protected them).

issue: Who found peace: Nanak himself (Manmohan Singh, Sant Singh Khalsa: Nanak has found peace; the Forgiver has forgiven him) or an unnamed subject with Nanak addressed (Darpan; Faridkot: those whom the Forgiver forgave found peace through the Guru's teaching).
our reading: O Nanak, through the Guru's teaching peace has been found; the Forgiver (himself) forgives.
alternatives: Through the Guru's teaching Nanak has found peace; the Forgiver has forgiven him.
decided because: The salok speaks of the fool and of those who follow the Guru, not of Nanak's own state; ਪਾਇਆ has no named subject, so style.md §12 makes Nanak vocative; ਬਖਸੇ is present (forgives), not a perfect.

issue: ਆਪਿ ਬੁਲਾਵੈ: calls (all) (Darpan: ਸਭ ਨੂੰ ਬੁਲਾਉਂਦਾ) or makes (all) speak (Manmohan Singh, Sant Singh Khalsa).
our reading: himself makes (all) speak / ਆਪ ਹੀ (ਜੀਵਾਂ ਤੋਂ) ਬੁਲਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ
alternatives: himself calls (all)
decided because: ਬੁਲਾਵੈ beside ਬੋਲੈ is its causative (he speaks, he causes to speak); both languages take the causative the pairing points to (ਜੀਵਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਬੁਲਾਉਂਦਾ, makes (all) speak).

issue: ਮਨ … ਪੜਿ ਰਹੀਐ: Faridkot reads ਮਨ as instrumental (with the mind we lie in your refuge) and ਹਰਿ as vocative; Darpan reads ਮਨ vocative with a command (ਪਿਆ ਰਹੁ).
our reading: O mind, let us stay fallen at the Lord's refuge.
alternatives: With the mind we lie in your refuge, O Lord; O mind, stay in the Lord's refuge.
decided because: The pauri's verbs are third person (ਮਾਰੈ, ਛੋਡੈ), so ਹਰਿ is not addressed; ਮਨ is vocative as in line 4; ਰਹੀਐ is the first-person plural optative, kept as let us (as ਜਪੀਐ ਮਨ ਮੇਰੇ at 89.3), not turned into a command. Lines 4 and 5 read the same.

issue: ਨਿਸਲੁ: Darpan and the Shabdarth: lying with legs stretched out, carefree; Santhya: from ਨਿਸ਼ਚਲ, motionless, the body let go; Faridkot: free of pain (ਦੁਖੋਂ ਸੇ ਰਹਿਤ); Manmohan Singh, Sant Singh Khalsa: fearless.
our reading: at ease, with limbs stretched out / ਲੱਤਾਂ ਪਸਾਰ ਕੇ ਅਰਾਮ ਨਾਲ
alternatives: fearless; free of pain; motionless
decided because: The Darpan, the Shabdarth and the Santhya agree on the bodily image of lying stretched out at ease, which completes ਨਿਚਿੰਦ; a note gives its sense.
